Mhlengi Gwala

By: Chuma Kave | Commission

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

Unique Selling Point:
After suffering numerous misfortunes including his amputated leg, Mhlengi Gwala fights to compete again.

Summary:
Mhlengi Gwala



After nearly losing his life, exactly 5 years ago, triathlete Mhlengi Gwala had to use every ounce of his strength to fight for his life first, to survive and to compete again. His story made international headlines in 2018 after criminals attacked him with a chainsaw that cut off 80% of his leg leaving him for dead. Two years later, in 2020, his leg caught infection and had to be amputated. Throughout all this, Mhlengi could only think of one way out…to go back to his old life of alcohol and drugs and totally forget about this dream - to be one of the top triathletes in the world.

It was three people who kept him away from a life of self-destruction; his mother, children, and friends - they kept reminding him of his greatness and that he could do it again. Sport, he says, is the only thing he knows, and without it life would have no meaning. It’s been a turbulent five years of stops and starts and in October 2023, he fnally picked his shoes to compete fully without any disruptions and to focus on his dreams; to compete in the 2024 Paralympics games. Mhlengi believes he will and is currently in the UAE and Australia for his Paralympic qualification.

Mhlengi hopes to forgive and forget the past five years which he considers the most horrible time of his life. On top of dealing with the trauma of his attack and losing his leg, he still faced more challenges like nearly losing his other good leg after an accident at work as a lifeguard and an almost a-year ban for a banned substance. Mhlengi still wonders if he will ever get justice as the criminals have never been caught.

Press Release:


Courageous Gwala
Mhlengi Gwala was an avid cyclist and a professional athlete. But one early morning in 2018, his entire life changed. Three assailants pulled him from his bicycle and attempted to saw off his leg with a chainsaw. They cut through meat and bone, leaving the limb barely attached to his body. Then, as suddenly as the attack began, his attackers disappeared into the darkness. Doctors managed to save his leg and Mhlengi bravely fought back to full recovery – only to lose his leg to infection two years later. Desperate to fulfil his dreams of becoming a champion triathlete, Mhlengi had to start all over again – this time, learning how to walk with one leg before he could swim, run and cycle. Now, he has set his sights on the Paris Paralympic Games later this year.

Producer: Chuma Kave | Presenter: Claire Mawisa

Script:


MHLENGI GWALA SCRIPT


INTRO
VIZ: The scene starts with Durban drone visuals that include the stadium
Cut to Mhlengi sitting on the bench holding a running shoe looking intense…
Upsound Mhlengi: I cry the most when I'm telling my story…
Visuals of Mhlengi riding a bike/visuals of him crossing the finish line - with crowd cheering….
Upsound TV (Sabc):…… “Gwala is facing a long period of recovery of two years…the doctors weren’t certain if he will be able to return to the sport he loves”
Upsound Mhlengi:…I'm here today. I'm still competing.

Link Claire: It’s a story that still sends shivers down my spine when I think about it. Six years ago, a young triathlete during one of his training sessions was brutally attacked by unknown assailants. The attackers had a chainsaw and attempted to saw off his leg while he was wide awake. That athletes name is Mhlengi Gwala

1. VO: On an early morning in March 2018, three people pulled Mhlengi from his bike, dragged him into a nearby bush and violently assaulted him.
Upsound Mhlengi:I tried to fight and I was crying and screaming…when I see that chainsaw rolling…and got to my leg.
2. VO: So brazen, so brutal was the incident that it made national and even international headlines…Why had his attackers seemed so determined to sever his leg?.... (PAUSE) Bleeding profusely, Mhlengi crawled to the main road and flagged down a passing security van.
Upsound Doctor: About 80% of the leg was actually severed.
3. VO: After hours of surgery, his leg was saved…
4. And remarkably, he made a strong recovery in the year after the attack, even competing in international triathlons – winning one.
5. But his relief would be short-lived.
6. In late 2019 – just over 18 months after the attack – a dull pain developed in his leg…
Mhlengi: It started with a small sore. So it kept going. I was going in and out of hospital,

Claire: Bona, what were they doing when you were in hospital? The doctors?

Mhlengi: I had the rod inside the bone. The first time they open and took the rod out because the rod was starting to rust by the knee. They tried to clean the wound and clean everything because there was a big wound on my on my ankle.

7. The initial reconstruction – using metal rods and pins – was no longer working, and Mhlengi was told he’d developed an infection that was devouring his leg…
Upsound Claire: So they say you need to amputate and you accept that decision?

Upsound Mhlengi:. I couldn’t fight it…it was the only option that I had…

8.

Mom: As time went by, we thought he was healing. But suddenly, they amputate his leg.
9. His mother, Bafundi Magwaza, found it hard to process the trauma of her son losing his leg…on top of the vivid memories of the days after the attack
Mom: I couldn’t eat the whole week, praying to the Lord, I really couldn’t figure out what I did to offend God

10. VO: It took months for Mhlengi’s wound to finally close. Still passionate about sports, he had to learn to walk... and then run... with a prosthesis.

Claire: Talk to me about the process of not just healing, but then getting prosthetics fitted and learning a new way of moving in life.

Mhlengi: There was a hard one. I was there in Darryl Grobbler…So the first time when they gonna make your leg…they have to model first. So there's a special bandage that you have to bandage on your stump for a month…I did that. And they take a mould…and they make a leg. When I came to fit it, I couldn’t make it.

Claire: What do you mean?

Mhlengi: I was crying, crying, crying. There’s pressure you have to fit in and …my stump is still new.
Claire: Too painful?
Mhlengi: Too painful… I can’t even walk.

11. VO: Mhlengi pushed through the pain, growing accustomed to his prosthetic leg. Darryl Grobbelaar was at his side, fitting his legs at no cost.

Upsound Darryl: He's special. He’s a real motivation. It’s good people…all providing their time and means for him to achieve that goal….the community rally behind him. It’s a great story. It’s a Durban story. It’s our story
Claire: Own it! I like that!


12: VO: Mhlengi later set his sights on getting back into the saddle, and now competes in international triathlon events. While training, he often rides past the site of his vicious attack.

Claire: How do you feel when you pass here?
Mhlengi: I just took the place and there's nothing I can change I can't feel bad. I can't feel happy.

Claire: How do you feel about the fact that they were never found?
Mhlengi: I'm not upset. I'm not happy. I’m ok

13. VO: It’s a pragmatic – even impressive answer – but it hides the anger Mhlengi clearly feels towards the people who attacked him and the frustration with those meant to bring them to justice. (PAUSE)

14. VO: In fact, frustration has become a theme in Mhlengi’s life. Just last year, having bounced back so courageously from the attack, he was dealt yet another blow.

Mom: He said, "Please allow me... I'm about to amputate my second leg." I said, "No! This can't happen. That foot is my last hope."


15. VO: While working as a lifeguard in eThekwini, a section of the shower block collapsed on top of him, badly injuring his good leg.
Claire: the wall fell on you?
Upsound Mhlengi: It was so bad…I took more than six months to seven months to close. I was in a vacuum machine for the wound for more than 6 months…. Smelling like…the wound can smell. Smelling! smelling!… I was so thin, thin, thin.
16. VO In hospital, with a wound that was severely infected and not healing, once again it was his mother who held him firmly.
Upsound Mhlengi: She’s so strong shem…she was strong from that day until today…so that woman is…ja!
Upsound Mom: When he is experiencing pain, I feel it too…. I carry his load all the time. Even when I'm on the streets, I can't even see where I am going.

17. His good leg eventually healed, Mhlengi went back to training, taking the ordeal as just another challenge.

Claire: How would you describe the last six years of your life?
Mhlengi: I would say 50/50. Challenging. Good. Happiness. Sadness. Lots of tears.


Link Claire: Mhlengi is so committed to being an elite international athlete that losing his leg hasn’t deterred him and now has his sights firmly set on the 2024 Paralympics in Paris
18. VO: To qualify for the global showpiece in France, Mhlengi has to accumulate sufficient points across a series of remaining races.
Upsound Claire: That’s a lot of pressure. Don’t you feel a bit stressed about that?
Upsound Mhlengi: It is. Most of the events happen in Europe. So travelling, money, stress, training. To travel alone you lose lots of energy on the plane and you get there…you’re tired….but I will make it.
Upsound Claire: I trust you will make it…that one I am not shocked about.
19. VO: As Mhlengi marches forward to the future, he continues to show his determination and that nothing can stand in his way.
Claire: So mama, what’s your greatest wish for him?
Upsound Mom: I wish him only the best. Whatever his heart desires. Even when he is out there competing, I pray for him until he returns home.
Mhlengi: I’m that kind of person, I will always find a way…I’m so in love with sports, so there’s always a way to do sports. (39942: 09:43)


PROMO SUGGESTIONS




PROMO 1 21”
A young triathlete, marred in a brutal attack.

UPS Mhlengi “ They said I won’t compete again”

But after six years of pure grit and determination, Mhlengi Gwala once again has his eye on gold.

UPS: I’m that kind of person, I will always find the way…There’s always a way. I’m so in love with sports. (39942: 09:43)




PROMO 2 21”

In 2018, three assailants attempted to hack off triathlete, Mhlengi Gwala’s leg

UPS “When you go inside there, that’s where they put the chainsaw and started cutting my legs. (39983: 2:20)

Now he is training hard, determined to make it to the Paralympic games in Paris, later this year.




PROMO 3 21”
In 2018 Mhlengi Gwala’s life changed forever…

UPS: Mhlengi
“ The only thing I remember is that they said I won’t compete again”

But six years later, he’s back on top and ready for the ultimate challenge – The Paralympics.

Claire: If that story doesn’t inspire you, I don’t know what will.”
